protocol: Leave-one-out over 12 anchors. 4 quartile-stratified calibration strips per case (selectStratifiedAnchors, never the target, rotation fixed across all runs). Target shots copied to a neutral /tmp/demoparty-cal/<label>/case-<hash>/ dir; child cwd there, outside the repo; only Read and Write exist (--tools). RECENT_SEVEN_BLOCK and MEDIAN_PIECE_BLOCK are NONE, so only absolute calibration is measured; the archiveEmpty:false path is covered by unit tests only. Verdicts checked with validateVerdictStrict(archiveEmpty true, expectedAnchors, requireScreenshotRef true). api_turns counts distinct assistant API messages in stream-json (what --max-turns limits); the CLI's num_turns counts content blocks.

m4b_findings: Run-to-run noise dominates: the same prompt and anchor rotation gave rho from 0.660 to 0.900.
Haiku compresses the scale (6 shipped runs): per-criterion SD vs agreed SD is ambition 3.2 vs 5.9, craft 2.2 vs 3.9, distinctness 2.0 vs 3.1; the 80 to 87 anchors land at 61 to 77.
anchor-12 (agreed 80) is underrated by 17 to 19 on every shipped run (61 to 63). anchor-01 (agreed 49) swings from 47 to 64 (median 58). No anchor-specific rule was added for either.
Head-to-head voting (iter2) made ranking worse (0.641, 0.607). Bottom-up criterion anchoring (iter3) lowered bias (about -2 vs -5) but not mean rho.

Aggregating jury calls helps: per-anchor median of runs 1 to 3 gives rho 0.9166, of runs 4 to 6 gives 0.7557, of all 6 gives 0.8757. A 3-sample median jury (about $0.01 per call) is the cheapest remaining lever; it is a pipeline change, not made here.
